cards.text: Stephen was one of seven men chosen to help with the church's daily food distribution, and now he stands before the Sanhedrin, the Jewish ruling council (Acts 6:3-5, 12). False witnesses say he never stops speaking against this holy place and against the law (Acts 6:13). Then the high priest asked Stephen, “Are these charges true?”
Stephen doesn't give a yes or a no. He says, “Brothers and fathers, listen to me!” and goes ALL the way back, like when you ask somebody how their day was and they start with the year they were born.

cards.question: Stephen starts with the God of glory appearing to the man he calls “our father,” back when he was still in Mesopotamia. Who is it?

cards.text: Abraham isn't even living in Haran yet when God speaks to him. God tells him, ‘Leave your country and your kindred and go to the land I will show you.’

cards.question: God tells Abraham the name of the land before he leaves home.

cards.text: No name, no map, just “the land I will show you,” and Abraham leaves the land of the Chaldeans and settles in Haran. Friend, I can't find my oven mitts without a map, and this man moves his WHOLE life.

cards.question: After Abraham's father dies, God brings him out of Haran. Where does God take him?

answers.text: Into the land the council lives in now
Down into the land of Egypt

cards.text: Here's the twist. God gives him no inheritance there, not even a foot of ground.

cards.question: Abraham doesn't own one foot of that land. But God promises to give it to Abraham and his ___, even though he doesn't have a ___ yet.

cards.text: Land for his kids, and the man has no kids and no land. That's a LOT of trust, and I used to lose hope just waiting on a drawer to open.

cards.question: God tells Abraham his descendants will settle into their land right away, with no hard years in between.

cards.text: Nope, God says they'll be foreigners in a strange land, enslaved and mistreated four hundred years. Four HUNDRED, and I thought a few years in a junk drawer was rough.

cards.question: God has more to say. He tells Abraham He will ___ the nation that enslaves his descendants.
After that, God says Abraham's descendants will come out of that strange land and worship Him where?

cards.text: Then God gives Abraham the covenant of circumcision. Abraham becomes the father of Isaac, Isaac of Jacob, and Jacob of the twelve patriarchs.

cards.question: The twelve patriarchs are Jacob's sons, and they sell their brother Joseph as a slave into Egypt. Why?

answers.text: Because they were jealous of him
Because their father told them to

cards.text: Sold by his own brothers. But God was with him and rescued him from all his troubles, while I got slid into one drawer and sulked for YEARS.

cards.question: God gives Joseph favor and wisdom in front of Pharaoh king of Egypt. What does Pharaoh make Joseph?

answers.text: Ruler over Egypt and his household

cards.text: Then famine and great suffering sweep across Egypt and Canaan. Jacob's family can't find food.

cards.question: With the famine on, Jacob hears there is ___ in Egypt.

cards.text: So Jacob sends his sons on their first visit to Egypt. The brothers who sold Joseph are walking into the country he rules, which is like showing up for a loan and the bank manager is the brother you SOLD.

cards.question: Joseph tells his brothers who he is on their very first visit to Egypt.

cards.text: On their second visit, Joseph reveals his identity, and Pharaoh learns about his family. Then Joseph sends for his father Jacob and all his relatives, seventy-five in all.

cards.question: After Jacob goes down to Egypt, he and his sons end up dying back home in Canaan.
Remember, God never gave Abraham even a foot of ground. When the bones of Jacob's family are carried back to Shechem, where are they placed?

answers.text: In a tomb Abraham bought there
In a cave Pharaoh gave them

cards.text: As the time nears for God to keep His promise to Abraham, the people in Egypt grow greatly in number. Then another king rises over Egypt who knew nothing of Joseph, like a new manager who's never heard of the guy who saved the company.

cards.question: This new king knows nothing of Joseph. How does he treat Israel's people in Egypt?

answers.text: He sends them home to Canaan

cards.text: He even forces them to abandon their infants so they would die. Right then a baby named Moses is born, and after three months in his father's house, he's set outside.

cards.question: Baby Moses is set outside. Who takes him and brings him up as her own son?
Growing up in Pharaoh's house, Moses is educated in all the wisdom of the ___.

cards.text: At forty years old, Moses decides to visit his brothers, the children of Israel. He sees one being mistreated, steps in, and strikes down the Egyptian who was oppressing him.

cards.question: After defending one of his people, Moses assumes his brothers will understand that God is using him to ___ them.

cards.text: But they did not understand. Moses thought everybody got the group chat, and nobody even knew there WAS a group chat.
The next day he finds two Israelites fighting and tries to make peace between them. He says, ‘Men, you are brothers. Why are you mistreating each other?’

cards.question: The man abusing his neighbor pushes Moses aside. What does he ask Moses?

answers.text: Who made him ruler and judge over them
Why he ever left Pharaoh's palace
Whether he works for the Egyptians

cards.text: Then the man adds, ‘Do you want to kill me as you killed the Egyptian yesterday?’ Uh oh, friend, yesterday's business is OUT.

cards.question: After that remark, where does Moses flee to live as a foreigner?

cards.text: Forty years go by. Then an angel appears to Moses in the flames of a burning bush in the desert near Mount Sinai.

cards.question: Moses marvels at the burning bush and walks up for a closer look. What comes to him?

cards.text: The Lord says, ‘I am the God of your fathers, the God of Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob.’ Moses trembles with fear and doesn't dare to look.

cards.question: Then the Lord tells Moses to take off his sandals. Why?

cards.text: Then the Lord says, ‘I have indeed seen the oppression of My people in Egypt. I have heard their groaning and have come down to deliver them.’

cards.question: The Lord tells Moses He will send him back to Egypt.

cards.text: Back to Egypt, the place he fled forty years before. That's like getting a call from the job you stormed out of, and they want you to start MONDAY.

cards.question: The man who pushed Moses aside asked, “Who made you ruler and judge?” Stephen says God sent that same Moses to be their ruler and ___.

cards.text: Moses leads them out, doing wonders and signs in Egypt, at the Red Sea, and for forty years in the wilderness. Forty when he visits his people, forty more before the bush, forty in the wilderness: this man's life runs on a forty-year timer.

cards.question: Stephen says this same Moses told the Israelites that God would raise up a prophet for them from among their brothers. A prophet like whom?
Stephen says Moses received living words to pass on to them. But their fathers refused to ___ him.
Stephen says that in their hearts, the fathers turned back to Egypt.

cards.text: They tell Aaron, Moses' brother (Exodus 4:14), ‘Make us gods who will go before us!’ They say they don't know what's happened to Moses, and they're already measuring his office.

cards.question: At that time, the people make a ___ and offer a sacrifice to it.

cards.text: And they rejoice in the works of their own hands. Friend, I'M the work of somebody's hands, and I promise you I never answered one single prayer.

cards.question: The people are celebrating an idol they made. How does God respond?

answers.text: He forgives them on the spot
He sends them back to Egypt

cards.text: God gives them over to the worship of the host of heaven. Then Stephen quotes God's words from the book of the prophets: ‘Did you bring Me sacrifices and offerings forty years in the wilderness, O house of Israel?’

cards.question: The prophecy goes on about the tabernacle of Molech and the star of Rephan, idols they made to worship. Where does God say He will send them?

answers.text: Out to the desert of Midian

cards.text: And that's where we'll leave it for now. Trust me, friend, Stephen is not done talking, and this story is not done either.

rule.text: He calls the baker "baker" or "friend," and talks to one baker at a time. Never "my baker," "kids" or "sweetie."

findings.problem: The included sermon Acts 7:2-43 doesn't have a stop of its own covering exactly those verses.

rule.text: An included parable or sermon (see passages.md) gets a stop of its own.

findings.problem: The card says Stephen was chosen to help with the church's daily food distribution and cites Acts 6:3-5, 12. The daily distribution and waiting on tables are in Acts 6:1-2, so that fact's reference doesn't cover where the text says it.

rule.text: Every Bible fact he states carries its reference.

findings.problem: The card quotes “the land I will show you” from Acts 7:3 but cites only Acts 7:4. It should cite Acts 7:3-4.

rule.text: Every story card cites the verses it tells, from the first verse it uses to the last, no wider and no narrower.

findings.problem: The second blank sits after "a" ("doesn't have a ___ yet"). That rules out the plural options and "money" on grammar alone, so only "child" and "wife" fit, and the right answers stand out by grammar instead of meaning.

rule.text: Don't let the right answer stand out. All the answers should sound alike.

findings.problem: This card only restates what cards 8 and 9 already told (no land, no child) and adds a joke, so it doesn't move the passage forward. It also says "That's a LOT of trust" as a fact about Abraham. Acts 7:5 says nothing about Abraham's trust, and the line isn't marked as Papa Dorin's own guess.
The joke sets God rescuing Joseph against Papa Dorin sulking in the drawer. Those aren't the same action, and the contrast suggests something about Joseph's attitude that Acts 7:9-10 never says.

rule.text: The everyday comparison must have the same action.

findings.problem: This is a where question, but the wrong answers "In a cave Pharaoh gave them" and "In a field Joseph conquered" are made up, not real details from the Bible.

rule.text: For who, which thing and where questions, wrong answers are real details from somewhere in the Bible, like Joppa when the right answer is Tarshish.

findings.problem: The card has four beats: infants abandoned, Moses born, three months in his father's house, and set outside. That's more than two. It should be split.

rule.text: Aim for one beat per story card. Two is the most. If a story card has more than two things happening, split it.

findings.problem: "Uh oh, friend, yesterday's business is OUT" is a mild throwaway that reads as pleasant, not funny, in a moment that could hold a real laugh.

rule.text: If a line reads like a nice dad being pleasant, push it further.

findings.problem: The card uses Moses fleeing (Acts 7:29) and the forty years (Acts 7:30) but cites only Acts 7:34. Also, "stormed out" doesn't match fleeing in fear after the man's remark, so the comparison's action is off.

rule.text: Every story card cites the verses it tells, from the first verse it uses to the last, no wider and no narrower.

findings.problem: The forty-year callback uses Acts 7:23 and 7:30, but the card cites only Acts 7:36.

rule.text: Every story card cites the verses it tells, from the first verse it uses to the last, no wider and no narrower.

findings.problem: "student" doesn't sound like something God would send Moses to be alongside "ruler." It's a weak, almost silly wrong answer that makes "redeemer" stand out.

rule.text: All the answers are the same kind of thing, about the same length and the same tone. None are silly.

findings.problem: The right answer (refused to obey) is only in Acts 7:39, but the card cites Acts 7:38-39.

rule.text: A choice card cites only the verses of its right answer.

findings.problem: The closing line copies the doc's example almost word for word ("And that's where we'll leave it for now. Trust me, friend, ... this story is not done") instead of being a new line.

rule.text: The examples show the idea. Write your own line each time.
